_note: The Modern Mirror: what each part of Atlantis is in the real world. 'rooms' shows in each building; 'topics' are the lessons a season report can pick (app/engine/report.py chooses which).

bank.text: Money for everyday spending. It earns little or nothing, and if a thief gets your debit card, it's this money they drain.
Pays interest and is protected: in the US, the FDIC insures bank deposits up to $250,000 if the bank fails. The catch is that savings interest often trails inflation.
7.5% a season is 30% a year. Average US card rates have sat above 20% a year, so a balance you carry grows fast.
A FICO score runs 300 to 850, just like Standing. Paying on time is the biggest part of it (35%), then how much of your limit you use (30%).
You put down a deposit and it becomes your limit. It's how people with no credit history, like newcomers to a country, start to build one.

market.text: Food is the bill you can't skip. Prices move with the seasons and with the news: US egg prices jumped in 2022 when bird flu hit the farms.
Gold pays no interest and no dividend, but it has held its value through centuries of rising prices. People buy it as a store of value, not to get rich.
Buy a lot of something and you push its price up. Big investment funds buy slowly for exactly this reason.

harbor.text: Where shares of companies are bought and sold. A share is a small piece of a company: when it does well, your piece is worth more.
A big, steady company that pays you a slice of its profits. Coca-Cola has raised its dividend every year for more than 60 years.
Big wins, big losses. Young tech companies can double in a year and halve the next.
A rare jackpot, and a loss on average. A big possible win makes the bet feel better than it is.
One purchase buys a little of the 500 biggest US companies, so one company's bad year barely dents it. Real index funds charge as little as 0.03% a year; the Tide Index's 1% a season would be steep.
The S&P 500 fell about 57% from 2007 to 2009, and 34% in a few weeks in 2020. People who had to sell then sold at the bottom.

harbor.there: A big goal, like a home down payment
harbor.text: It has to be paid in cash on the day. Shares that are worth enough on paper don't count until you've sold them.

guild_hall.text: Steady, reliable, and slow. Wages usually rise a little each year, while big goals like a home can get dearer faster.
Time is a budget too. An hour spent one way can't be spent another: economists call that the opportunity cost.
Saving from wages alone rarely keeps up with rising prices. Money that earns its own return is what closes the gap.

drowned_bell.text: Every game is built to pay back less than it takes; that difference is the house edge. US state lotteries pay out roughly half to two-thirds of what they sell in prizes.
A few big wins keep people playing. The wheel pays back 88 coins for every 100 staked, about what many slot machines do.
In 2021 GameStop shares went from about $20 to over $400 on internet hype, then fell back. A tip that's right 7 times in 10 is still wrong 3 times.

black_reef.text: A typical two-week payday loan costs $15 for every $100 borrowed, close to 400% a year. Most borrowers end up renewing it rather than paying it off.
The easy yes is the trap. Lenders who don't check whether you can repay charge enough to profit when you can't.

circle.text: Neighbours pool money and take turns receiving the pot. They're called tandas in Mexico, susus in West Africa and the Caribbean, chit funds in India and hui in China.
You get the money now and pay it back over time, with no interest, just trust. Some US nonprofits even report circle payments to the credit bureaus, so they build a credit score.

council.text: In the US the Federal Reserve sets interest rates and aims to keep inflation near 2% a year. The government sets taxes.
A bill that comes every year whatever you earned. It has to be planned for.
Roman emperors cut the silver in their coins until the denarius was mostly bronze, and prices soared. US inflation hit 9.1% in 2022. Cash buys less; houses, shares and gold tend to rise with prices.

payday_loan.name: Payday loans
payday_loan.text: Grin is a payday lender. A typical two-week payday loan charges $15 per $100, close to 400% a year, and most borrowers renew it instead of paying it off. It's the costliest money there is.

ponzi.name: Ponzi schemes
ponzi.text: The Pearl Exchange paid nobody: early 'returns' come from later investors' money. Bernie Madoff ran one for decades and investors lost billions. A guaranteed high return is the clearest warning sign there is.

missed_payment.name: Payment history
missed_payment.text: Paying on time is the biggest part of a credit score, about 35% of FICO. One payment 30 days late can stay on a credit report for seven years.

card_interest.name: Credit card interest
card_interest.text: Card interest compounds: next season you pay interest on this season's interest. US cards have averaged over 20% a year. Paying only the minimum can stretch a small balance over years.

card_fraud.name: Disputing charges
card_fraud.text: Check your statement. In the US you can dispute a credit card billing error within 60 days, and most cards cover fraud in full. Debit card fraud protection shrinks the longer you wait to report it.

house_edge.name: The house edge
house_edge.text: Every casino game pays back less than it takes, on average. You can win a night; you can't win a year. US lotteries pay out roughly half to two-thirds of ticket sales in prizes.

cash_theft.name: Keeping cash safe
cash_theft.text: Cash can be lost or stolen, and nobody gives it back. Money in a US bank is insured by the FDIC up to $250,000, which is why most people keep only what they'll spend soon in their wallet.

inflation.name: Inflation
inflation.text: The debasement made every price jump while your coin stayed the same. That's inflation: US prices rose 9.1% in the year to June 2022. Cash loses value, while assets like homes, shares and gold tend to rise with prices.

emergency_fund.name: Emergency funds
emergency_fund.text: Roofs leak when they want to. In a 2023 Federal Reserve survey, more than a third of US adults said they couldn't cover a $400 surprise with cash. Planners suggest keeping three to six months of costs saved.

lottery.name: Lottery stocks
lottery.text: Deepcoral wins rarely and loses on average, like penny stocks. People overpay for a small chance at a big win, which is exactly why the bet is bad.

index_fund.name: Index funds
index_fund.text: The Tide Index is like an S&P 500 index fund: one purchase spreads your money over many companies, so one bad voyage barely matters. Real ones charge as little as 0.03% a year.

diversify.name: Diversification
diversify.text: All your shares rode on one house. When Enron collapsed in 2001, many of its workers lost their jobs and their retirement savings at once, because both were in Enron.

dividends.name: Dividends
dividends.text: Some companies pay shareholders part of their profits, as Oro & Daughters does after a good voyage. Reinvested over years, dividends make up a large share of what the stock market returns.

rosca.name: Lending circles
rosca.text: Old Maro's circle is a ROSCA: tandas, susus, chit funds, hui. Millions of people use them worldwide to save and borrow without a bank, and some US nonprofits report the payments to credit bureaus.

seasonal_prices.name: Buying ahead
seasonal_prices.text: You bought kelp before it got dear. Buying food in season, or in bulk when it's cheap, is one of the simplest ways households stretch a budget.

opportunity_cost.name: Opportunity cost
opportunity_cost.text: An unused tide isn't free; it costs the shift you didn't work. Economists call the value of the best thing you gave up the opportunity cost.

credit_score.name: Credit scores
credit_score.text: Standing works like a FICO score: on-time payments matter most, then using little of your limit (under 30% is the usual advice), then how long you've had accounts. Building it takes time.

savings_rate.name: Savings and inflation
savings_rate.text: Your Vault earned interest, but less than Passage rose. Savings accounts often trail inflation: for most of the 2010s the average US savings account paid under 0.1% a year while prices rose about 2%.

news_shock.name: News moves markets
news_shock.text: When the Ever Given got stuck in the Suez Canal in 2021, it held up billions of dollars of trade a day and shipping prices leapt. Surprises like that are why no single bet is safe.

real_return.name: Real returns
real_return.text: What counts is how much faster your money grows than prices. Earn 5% while prices rise 3% and you're only 2% better off. Passage rising every season is the inflation you're racing.
